```json
{
  "title": "Project setup: git rules, environment variables and the server package",
  "summary": "Build the foundation files before any server code exists. You write a .gitignore so private and generated files never enter git, a .env.example that documents which settings the server needs (with safe placeholder values), a real .env for your own machine that stays private, and server/package.json that names the server and lists the libraries it will use. Level 0 gave you README.md; this level adds the rules and setup that every later server file (server/index.js, the database code, the auth code) will rely on. No JavaScript logic is written yet.",
  "files_to_write": [
    {
      "path": ".gitignore",
      "purpose": "Tells git which things to never track: the installed packages folder (node_modules), the private .env file, any SQLite database files (anything ending in .db), and the front-end build output folder (dist). Each entry goes on its own line."
    },
    {
      "path": ".env.example",
      "purpose": "A safe, committed template that lists the three environment variable names the server will need: PORT, JWT_SECRET and DATABASE_FILE. It uses harmless placeholder values (a port number, an obvious 'change me' style secret, and a database file name ending in .db) so a new developer knows what to fill in. It must never contain a real secret."
    },
    {
      "path": ".env",
      "purpose": "Your private local copy of the same three variables with values you choose for your own machine. It must use the same variable names as .env.example. For JWT_SECRET, use a long random-looking string that is different from the placeholder. This file is never committed to git because .gitignore excludes it."
    },
    {
      "path": "server/package.json",
      "purpose": "Describes the server as an npm package: a name for it, a version, index.js as the main entry file, a 'start' script that runs index.js with Node, and a dependencies list containing exactly these six libraries: bcrypt, better-sqlite3, cors, dotenv, express and jsonwebtoken. Use caret version ranges that allow compatible updates (bcrypt 5.x, better-sqlite3 11.x, cors 2.x, dotenv 16.x, express 4.x, jsonwebtoken 9.x). It must be valid JSON."
    }
  ],
  "inputs": [
    "Commands you run yourself: npm install inside the server/ folder, and git status or git check-ignore from the repo root to test your ignore rules.",
    "Environment variable names the later server code will read: PORT (which port the server listens on), JWT_SECRET (the secret used to sign login tokens), DATABASE_FILE (the SQLite file name).",
    "Your own choice of values for the private .env file (a port, a secret string, a database file name)."
  ],
  "outputs": [
    "A .gitignore that makes git skip node_modules, .env, any *.db file and dist.",
    "A committed .env.example showing PORT, JWT_SECRET and DATABASE_FILE with placeholder values only.",
    "A private .env with the same three names and your own values, which does not show up in git status as a new file to add.",
    "server/package.json that is valid JSON, so running npm install in server/ finishes without errors and creates a node_modules folder (and a lock file) inside server/.",
    "Running npm start in server/ is allowed to fail at this stage because index.js does not exist yet; the script only needs to be declared."
  ],
  "acceptance_checks": [
    {
      "id": "A1",
      "description": "npm install succeeds in server/ and the package.json declares the right name, entry file, start script and the six dependencies.",
      "how_to_verify": "Open server/package.json and confirm it has a name, a version, main pointing to index.js, a start script that runs index.js with node, and exactly the six dependencies bcrypt, better-sqlite3, cors, dotenv, express and jsonwebtoken. Then run 'npm install' inside server/ and check that it ends without errors and that a node_modules folder appears."
    },
    {
      "id": "A2",
      "description": "Git ignores .env, node_modules, *.db files and dist, but does not ignore .env.example.",
      "how_to_verify": "Run 'git check-ignore -v .env server/node_modules todos.db dist' from the repo root and confirm all four are reported as ignored. Run 'git check-ignore .env.example' and confirm it prints nothing (meaning it is NOT ignored). Also run 'git status' and confirm .env and node_modules are not listed as untracked files."
    },
    {
      "id": "A3",
      "description": "The .env.example and .env files list the same three variable names, and .env.example holds only placeholder values, no real secret.",
      "how_to_verify": "Read both files side by side and confirm each has PORT, JWT_SECRET and DATABASE_FILE (one per line, NAME=value format, no spaces around =). Check that the JWT_SECRET in .env.example is an obvious placeholder, and that the JWT_SECRET in .env is a different value that you chose."
```
